title: Corelight Connector Exporter
descriptionMarkdown: The [Corelight](https://corelight.com/) data connector enables incident responders and threat hunters who use Microsoft Sentinel to work faster and more effectively. The data connector enables ingestion of events from [Zeek](https://zeek.org/) and [Suricata](https://suricata.io/) via Corelight Sensors into Microsoft Sentinel using the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API. Events are sent by the Corelight Sensor to a Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) and routed into dedicated `Corelight_v3_*_CL` tables by per-log-type Data Collection Rules (DCRs).
additionalRequirementBanner: This data connector depends on a parser based on a Kusto Function to work as expected [**Corelight**](https://aka.ms/sentinel-Corelight-parser) which is deployed with the Microsoft Sentinel Solution.

sampleQueries.query:
Corelight
	| summarize count() by id_orig_h
	| top 10 by count_

sampleQueries.description: Connection events over the last 24 hours
sampleQueries.query:
Corelight_v3_conn_CL
	| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
	| summarize count() by bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)

union withsource=TableName Corelight_v3_*_CL
	| summarize EventCount = count(), LastReceived = max(TimeGenerated) by TableName
	| sort by EventCount desc

value:
Corelight_v3_conn_CL
	| summarize LastLogReceived = max(TimeGenerated)
	| project IsConnected = LastLogReceived > ago(30m)

resourceProvider.permissionsDisplayText: read and write permissions are required.

read and write permissions to Data Collection Rules and Data Collection Endpoints are required. [See the documentation to learn more about the Logs Ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview).

customs.name: Microsoft Entra ID application
customs.description: Permission to register an application in Microsoft Entra ID and create a client secret. Typically requires the Application Developer role or higher.

customs.name: Azure role assignment
customs.description: Permission to assign the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role on the deployed Data Collection Rules. Typically requires the Owner or User Access Administrator role on the target resource group.

customs.name: Corelight Sensor access
customs.description: Administrative access to the Corelight Sensor (or Fleet Manager) to configure the Microsoft Sentinel export.

instructionSteps.description: >**NOTE:** This data connector depends on a parser based on a Kusto Function to work as expected [**Corelight**](https://aka.ms/sentinel-Corelight-parser) which is deployed with the Microsoft Sentinel Solution.

instructionSteps.title: 1. Deploy the Corelight data collection resources
instructionSteps.description: Deploy the ARM template that creates the Data Collection Endpoint (DCE), the `Corelight_v3_*_CL` tables, and one Data Collection Rule (DCR) per Corelight log type in your workspace.

parameters.content:
Use the button below to deploy the connector resources into the same subscription and resource group as your Microsoft Sentinel workspace.

[![Deploy to Azure](https://aka.ms/deploytoazurebutton)](https://aka.ms/sentinel-CorelightExporter-azuredeploy)

When prompted, supply:

| Parameter | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `workspace` | The **name** of your Log Analytics workspace (not the ID) |
| `workspace-location` | The Azure region of the workspace |
| `resourceId` | The full resource ID of the workspace |

The deployment creates:

- One Data Collection Endpoint named `dce-corelight-<workspace>`
- One custom table per Corelight log type, named `Corelight_v3_<log_type>_CL`
- One Data Collection Rule per log type, named `dcr-corelight-<workspace>-<log_type>`, each tagged with `corelight-log-type`

> **NOTE:** The deployment can take several minutes to complete because a large number of tables and rules are created. Wait for it to finish before continuing.

instructionSteps.title: 2. Register a Microsoft Entra ID application
instructionSteps.description: The Corelight Sensor authenticates to the Logs Ingestion API with a Microsoft Entra ID application. Create the application and a client secret, then record the values.

parameters.content:
#### Create the application

1. In the Azure portal, go to **Microsoft Entra ID** > **App registrations** > **New registration**.
2. Enter a name, for example `Corelight Sentinel Connector`.
3. Under **Supported account types**, select **Accounts in this organizational directory only**.
4. Leave **Redirect URI** empty and select **Register**.
5. On the application **Overview** page, copy the **Application (client) ID** and the **Directory (tenant) ID**.

#### Create a client secret

1. On the application page, go to **Certificates & secrets** > **Client secrets** > **New client secret**.
2. Enter a description, choose an expiry, and select **Add**.
3. Copy the secret **Value** immediately. It is shown only once and cannot be retrieved later.

You now have the **Tenant ID**, **Client ID**, and **Client Secret** required by the Corelight Sensor.

For more information, see [Register an application with Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app).

instructionSteps.title: 3. Grant the application permission to send data
instructionSteps.description: Assign the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role so the application can publish to the Data Collection Rules created in step 1.

parameters.content:
Assign the role once at the **resource group** scope so it covers every Corelight Data Collection Rule in a single assignment.

1. Go to the resource group that contains the deployed DCE and DCRs.
2. Select **Access control (IAM)** > **Add** > **Add role assignment**.
3. On the **Role** tab, search for and select **Monitoring Metrics Publisher**.
4. On the **Members** tab, choose **User, group, or service principal**, then select the application you registered in step 2.
5. Select **Review + assign**.

Alternatively, assign the role with the Azure CLI:

```bash
az role assignment create \
  --assignee <client-id> \
  --role "Monitoring Metrics Publisher" \
  --scope /subscriptions/<subscription-id>/resourceGroups/<resource-group>
```

> **NOTE:** Role assignments can take a few minutes to take effect. If the sensor reports authorization errors immediately after assignment, wait and retry.

instructionSteps.title: 4. Collect the Data Collection Endpoint and Rule identifiers
instructionSteps.description: The Corelight Sensor needs the DCE ingestion URI and the immutable ID of each Data Collection Rule it sends to.

parameters.content:
#### Data Collection Endpoint URI

1. Go to **Monitor** > **Settings** > **Data Collection Endpoints**.
2. Select `dce-corelight-<workspace>`.
3. On the **Overview** page, copy the **Logs ingestion** URI. It has the form `https://dce-corelight-<workspace>-<suffix>.<region>.ingest.monitor.azure.com`.

#### Data Collection Rule immutable IDs

Each Corelight log type has its own DCR and its own immutable ID. To retrieve the DCRs with their log type, run:

```bash
az monitor data-collection rule list \
  --resource-group <resource-group> \
  --query "[?tags.solution=='Corelight'].{logType:tags.\"corelight-log-type\", immutableId:immutableId, name:name}" \
  --output table
```

To look up a single log type, for example `conn`:

```bash
az monitor data-collection rule show \
  --resource-group <resource-group> \
  --name dcr-corelight-<workspace>-conn \
  --query immutableId --output tsv
```

You can also read the immutable ID in the portal: **Monitor** > **Data Collection Rules** > select the rule > **JSON View** > `immutableId`.

#### Stream names

Each DCR declares a single stream, named after its destination table:

```
Custom-<table_name>
```

For most log types the table name follows the pattern `Corelight_v3_<log_type>_CL`. For example, the `conn` log type uses the stream `Custom-Corelight_v3_conn_CL` and lands in the table `Corelight_v3_conn_CL`.

> **IMPORTANT:** A small number of log types with long names have a shortened table name, because Log Analytics limits table name length. For those log types the stream name is **not** `Custom-Corelight_v3_<log_type>_CL`. For example, the `opcua_binary_create_monitored_items` log type uses the stream `Custom-Corelight_v3_opcua_binary_cm_items_CL`. Always read the stream name from the DCR itself rather than deriving it from the log type:
>
> ```bash
> az monitor data-collection rule show \
>   --resource-group <resource-group> \
>   --name dcr-corelight-<workspace>-<log_type> \
>   --query "keys(streamDeclarations)" --output tsv
> ```

instructionSteps.title: 5. Configure the Corelight Sensor
instructionSteps.description: Configure the Microsoft Sentinel export on the Corelight Sensor with the values collected in the previous steps.

parameters.content:
Contact your Corelight TAM, SE, or [info@corelight.com](mailto:info@corelight.com) for the Microsoft Sentinel export package and configuration guidance for your sensor version.

Configure the export with:

| Setting | Where it comes from |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant ID | Step 2, application **Directory (tenant) ID** |
| Client ID | Step 2, application **Application (client) ID** |
| Client Secret | Step 2, client secret **Value** |
| DCE ingestion URI | Step 4, Data Collection Endpoint **Logs ingestion** URI |
| DCR immutable ID | Step 4, immutable ID for the log type being sent |
| Stream name | `Custom-Corelight_v3_<log_type>_CL` |

Enable only the log types you intend to ingest. Each enabled log type is sent to the DCR and stream that match its name.

> **NOTE:** Ingesting a large number of log types increases Microsoft Sentinel data ingestion cost. Review the [Microsoft Sentinel pricing](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/microsoft-sentinel/) page before enabling the full set.

instructionSteps.title: 6. Verify data ingestion
instructionSteps.description: Confirm that events from the Corelight Sensor are arriving in your workspace.

parameters.content:
Allow 5 to 15 minutes after configuring the sensor for the first events to appear, then run the following queries in **Logs**.

Check which Corelight tables are receiving data:

```kusto
union withsource=TableName Corelight_v3_*_CL
| summarize EventCount = count(), LastReceived = max(TimeGenerated) by TableName
| sort by LastReceived desc
```

Check connection events specifically:

```kusto
Corelight_v3_conn_CL
| take 10
```

Confirm connectivity:

```kusto
Corelight_v3_conn_CL
| summarize LastLogReceived = max(TimeGenerated)
| project IsConnected = LastLogReceived > ago(30m)
```

If no data appears, verify that the role assignment from step 3 has taken effect, that the DCR immutable ID matches the log type being sent, and that the stream name is spelled exactly as `Custom-Corelight_v3_<log_type>_CL`.
